brief.title: Red Wine Quality Classification
brief.purpose: Build and compare machine-learning classifiers that predict red-wine quality from the supplied physicochemical dataset, then write a grounded university-project report.
brief.current_focus: Prepare reproducible exploratory data analysis before choosing the label and evaluation strategy.
recent_progress: Inspected its row count, schema, missing cells, target values, and checksum.
key_constraints: Use ml_project/winequality-red.csv as the project dataset.
Treat quality prediction as a classification problem.
Do not claim model results unless they come from recorded reproducible runs.
open_questions: Should quality remain a six-class target or be grouped into broader quality bands?
Which split strategy and imbalance-aware metrics should be used for model comparison?
next_actions: Run exploratory data analysis and record its artefacts.
Propose the label, split, preprocessing, baseline, and evaluation strategy for user confirmation.

memories.content: The project goal is to compare machine-learning classifiers for red-wine quality and produce a report grounded in the recorded analysis and model runs.
The dataset is ml_project/winequality-red.csv with 1,599 rows, 11 numeric predictor columns, and the target column quality.
The initial inspection found no blank cells and target counts of 3:10, 4:53, 5:681, 6:638, 7:199, and 8:18; label grouping remains an open post-EDA decision.
